case_name: Ameer-Un-Nissa Begum and Others v Mahboob Begum and Others
facts: The dispute between the parties relates to rights of succession to the 'matrooka' or personal estate left by one Nawab Wali-ud-Dowlah, a wealthy noble man and a high dignitary in the State of Hyderabad.

Ameer-un-nissa Begam, appellant 1 in the appeals before us, was one of the wedded wives of the Nawab and that she and the five children, whom she bore to her husband, are entitled to their legitimate shares in the properties left by the deceased.
Fatima-un-nissa Begum left her husband's house a few months after her marriage but the marriage was never dissolved.

The controversy between the parties really centred round the point as to whether two other ladies, to wit, Mahboob Begum and Quadiran Begum were legally married wives of the late Nawab, or whether they were mere 'kavases'or permanent concubines kept by him.
issues: Whether Mahboob Begum and Quadiran Begum were legally married wives of the Nawab
Whether Fatima-un-nissa Begum was a legally wedded wife of the Nawab
court_reasoning: The Commission submitted its report on 16-10-1944.

They found that Mahboob Begum and Quadiran were both legally married wives of the Nawab, with the result that they and their children were entitled to participate in the distribution of the 'matrooka'.
Fatimaunnissa was also held to be a legally wedded wife of the Nawab and as such entitled to the dower claimed by her.
holding: The Nizam directed that the report of the Special Commission should be scrutinised by an Advisory Committee consisting of three persons, to wit, two Judges of the High Court and the Legal Adviser of the State.

The 'Firman' is in these terms : 'In this connection even after knowing the opinion of the advisers who were appointed to advise the members of the Council, the opinion of the majority of the Council is that the decision of the Commission is worthy of being implemented.'
